articles.title: New Manchester United boss Pochettino ‘doesn’t need too much preparation’ for Liverpool opener
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has indicated he knows enough about Liverpool to not be concerned at the short turnaround prior to his first game in charge of Manchester United on Sunday
articles.content:
New Manchester United boss Pochettino ‘doesn’t need too much preparation’ for Liverpool opener

Mauricio Pochettino has indicated he knows enough about Liverpool to not be concerned at the short turnaround prior to his first game in charge of Manchester United on Sunday

Last Update:

Mauricio Pochettino is not concerned at the short turnaround between leaving his role as head coach of the United States and the start of his job at Manchester United, and insisted he won’t spend too much time preparing a dossier on weekend opponents Liverpool.

Pochettino was last week named the new United boss, succeeding the sacked Michael Carrick, and will take over once his commitments with US Soccer are completed.

His final game in charge of the US is Tuesday night’s CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final, second leg against Haiti in Cincinnati, after which he will make a trans-Atlantic dash to assume his new position at Old Trafford.

The circumstances mean he will have little time with his new players before Sunday’s trip to Anfield but the Argentine is not concerned.

Asked how difficult it is to switch from focusing on the US to United, he said: “For me, it’s not difficult. I think we are well prepared to switch quickly from the national team to the clubs, from one game you know you need to play well to another that you need to be ready again, from one action to the next action. I think we are well prepared.

“All the experience from the past helps us to be focused on the priority of the moment.  For sure, in the moment that we finish that game, we are going to start to be 100% focused on our next project. If you say to me, I need to go here, there, there, Argentina, or I don’t know, Mexico, or Canada… we watch soccer every day in all the leagues because that is our passion. We know very well the teams and I don’t think we need too much preparation about the opponent. The most important [thing] is to know the details about our players, our staff, our culture, our identity, and from there to improve.”

United States set to enjoy Pochettino’s final game before United switch

The US won the first leg 6-0 against Haiti in Miami and are a shoo-in to reach the last four.

Pochettino, whose number two Jesus Perez left the US camp on Saturday night to head to Manchester along with assistant Toni Jiménez and fitness coach and son Sebastiano Pochettino, has been with the US for 26 months but would not be drawn on whether he will look to sign the team’s better players when he gets to United.

He added: “Now it’s not time. I know that you asked the players before. All good players always have dreams.

“To reach the last level, and I see United as one of the teams that is in the last level…it’s a dream for many of the players. But now I see they need to be focusing on today, on tomorrow’s game, on their clubs.

“I know really well for more than two years every single player, and I see they are all players with an unbelievable talent. And of course, in the future when that happens, we are going to pay attention.”

Inevitable that US players will now be linked with Manchester United – McKennie

USA midfielder Weston McKennie, who plays for Juventus, said it was inevitable that players would be linked with a switch to Old Trafford.

He said: “He’s obviously grown to like this team and seeing the quality that this team has to offer. I think it has potential.

“I think you know we have a lot of guys on our team that are due to make moves soon or within the next year. And so I think it’s kind of inevitable. But at the end of the day, you never know what’s going on in coach’s mind and what players he’s actually looking for. I think he could potentially see some of the guys from here being talked about to go to Man U and potentially it happening.”

articles.title: FFF chief Diallo to stand against Infantino in FIFA presidential election
articles.summary: A credible candidate has finally stepped forward to take on Gianni Infantino in the FIFA presidential election
articles.content:
FFF chief Diallo to stand against Infantino in FIFA presidential election

A credible candidate has finally stepped forward to take on Gianni Infantino in the FIFA presidential election

Last Update:

Philippe Diallo will stand as the UEFA-backed candidate in the FIFA presidential election in March.

Diallo, the president of the French Football Federation, was invited to stand by the UEFA Executive Committee as they look to find a way to end the reign of Gianni Infantino.

European football’s governing body is desperate for Infantino to be replaced following his proposal to sell off stakes in the governing body’s competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors. It was also unhappy with FIFA for overturning United States striker Folarin Balogun’s red card at the World Cup following the intervention of US president Donald Trump.

A UEFA statement on Monday read: “At a meeting held today and chaired by UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin, the national associations represented on the UEFA Executive Committee invited Philippe Diallo, president of the French Football Federation (FFF), to stand as a candidate in the FIFA presidential election in March 2027 and unanimously pledged their full support.

“Philippe Diallo has extensive experience across all levels of the game, having led the organisation representing French professional football clubs, served on the board of the French professional league and within FIFA’s dispute resolution structures, before becoming President of the FFF and a member of the UEFA Executive Committee in 2023.

“Against the backdrop of serious concerns over the direction of FIFA, the national associations called for renewed unity and trust within the global football community. They also called for a FIFA that places the development of the game in every region of the world at the heart of its mission, upholds the highest standards of governance and works in close partnership with its member associations, confederations and football stakeholders. They expressed their full confidence in Philippe Diallo to provide the leadership needed to achieve this ambition.

“Philippe Diallo has accepted the invitation to stand. His candidacy is due to be formally ratified by the FFF Executive Committee at its meeting tomorrow.”

Infantino favourite to retain FIFA presidency

Challengers to Infantino have to declare their intention to run ahead of the November 18 deadline. They have been few and far between so far with only former Switzerland international Ramon Vega putting himself forward, although there is uncertainty as to whether he meets the necessary criteria. There have been reports FIFA Council member Kozo Tashima could challenge.

Whoever stands will have a difficult task in trying to oust Infantino, who has been in charge since February 2016. The Swiss is the overwhelming favourite to secure a fourth term as the most powerful man in football.

That is not a scenario Germany’s former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp finds palatable. Klopp described Infantino as worse than disgraced former FIFA chief Seep Blatter, who resigned in 2015 amidst a corruption scandal.

“I’ve been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense,” said Klopp.

“I didn’t think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that.”

Klopp wants someone who cares about football and not finance to run FIFA

Klopp added: “Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job.

“There are people who truly care about the future of football – people who aren’t driven by financial interests. If someone like that were to step up – if someone like that were to become president – I think that would be a significant improvement.

“There are surely people who care deeply about the future of football and have no financial interests in it.”

articles.title: Belgium striker Romelu Lukaku quits international football
articles.summary: Romelu Lukaku walks away from international football as Belgium's all-time leading goalscorer
articles.content:
Belgium striker Romelu Lukaku quits international football

Romelu Lukaku walks away from international football as Belgium's all-time leading goalscorer

Last Update:

Romelu Lukaku has announced his international retirement after 135 caps and 94 goals for Belgium.

The 33-year-old, who plays his club football for Turkish side Fenerbahce, confirmed he would be stepping back in a post on Instagram this morning, just 12 hours after failing to come off the bench as Belgium beat Italy 4-1 in the Nations League.

He wrote: “These 16 years I gave all I had for the national team…I went through every emotion possible.

“I played with amazing team-mates that I will always be grateful for. I want to thank them all. I want to thank all the coaches as well for pushing and trusting me to help the team. It was a nice ride and I enjoyed every single moment.

“To the Belgium fans thank you for the support you gave our team. I am proud to have represented my country in four World Cups and three European Championships. I will never forget those moments, I’m at peace with my decision to stop here.

“It was amazing, it was enjoyable, I’m grateful, thank you.”

Lukaku was more than a goalscorer – Belgian FA

Lukaku is Belgium’s record goalscorer having made his international debut aged 16.

A statement from the Royal Belgian Football Association read: “The Royal Belgian Football Association would like to express its sincere gratitude to Romelu Lukaku for his exceptional contribution to the history of the Belgian Red Devils and Belgian football.

“Since making his international debut on 3 March 2010, at just 16 years of age, Romelu has earned an impressive 135 caps for the national team and scored 94 goals. These exceptional figures make him the Belgian Red Devils’ all-time leading goalscorer.

“During his international career spanning more than 16 years, he represented Belgium at four FIFA World Cups (2014, 2018, 2022 and 2026) and three UEFA European Championships (2016, 2020 and 2024). He notably played a key role in Belgium’s historic third-place finish at the 2018 FIFA World Cup in Russia.

“But Romelu Lukaku was much more than just a goalscorer. Through his personality, leadership, dedication and strong connection to the national team, he has earned a special place in the history of the Belgian Red Devils.

“His journey, from making his debut at just 16 years old to competing on the biggest international stages, remains a tremendous source of inspiration for countless young footballers and children who dream of one day wearing the Belgium shirt themselves.

“The Royal Belgian Football Association would like to extend its heartfelt thanks to Romelu for all these years, for the emotions he has shared with the fans and for the unforgettable memories he leaves behind.

“We wish him all the very best for the remainder of his professional career, but above all, happiness, fulfilment and many wonderful moments in his personal life, surrounded by his loved ones.

“Thank you for everything, Romelu. You will always be a Belgian Red Devil.”

Mignolet – we are grateful for Lukaku’s contribution

The Belgian FA’s technical director Simon Mignolet added: “Romelu has meant an enormous amount to the Belgian Red Devils for more than 16 years. Beyond his exceptional performances on the pitch, he was a true leader, with a strong personality and an important presence in the dressing room.

“We respect his decision and are deeply grateful for everything he has contributed to our national team. Today, a new generation is ready to carry the team forward, thanks in part to the legacy he leaves behind. We must now look ahead and prepare for the Nations League quarter-finals, with the ambition of continuing to grow as a team.”

articles.title: Romario talks a lot! Ancelotti takes subtle swipe at former Brazil striker
articles.summary: Brazil's recent performances have drawn plenty of criticism, including from former striker Romario, but national team boss Carlo Ancelotti is unconcerned
articles.content:
Romario talks a lot! Ancelotti takes subtle swipe at former Brazil striker

Brazil's recent performances have drawn plenty of criticism, including from former striker Romario, but national team boss Carlo Ancelotti is unconcerned

Last Update:

Carlo Ancelotti has refused to engage in a war of words with Romario but claimed the former Brazil striker “talks a lot”.

Romario made 70 appearances for his country, scoring 55 goals, as part of a glittering career that also took in spells with PSV Eindhoven, Barcelona, Flamengo and Vasco da Gama. He is now a politician and quick to air his views.

He pointed the finger at Ancelotti following Brazil’s 3-2 defeat to Japan on Saturday, writing on Instagram: “Ancelotti, it’s done! Take your things and go. Nobody is questioning your history. You’re one of the greatest coaches the world has ever seen, but that was in club football. With the Brazil national team, so far, things haven’t been the same. We can’t take it much longer.

“Do you want to continue coaching? Go back to the clubs where you made your name, because the Brazil national team can’t keep paying for it.”

Brazil boss Ancelotti unperturbed by Romario words

Ancelotti, who was sent off in the defeat to Japan after taking his complaints about the refereeing too far, acknowledged Romario’s words but opted against biting back.

The Italian said: ”It’s freedom of expression, and in a democratic country, everyone can have an opinion. Romario gave his and everyone has the right to tell lies, truths or nonsense. The truth is that Romario talks a lot, and that’s his right.”

Brazil suffered a disappointing round-of-16 exit to Norway at the World Cup and Ancelotti has used the subsequent period to try out new players but admitted he needed to combine that with better results.

He added: ”It’s a new job, I really like what we’re doing, but I don’t think it’s enough. I have to do more and I will. I like being here, I like being with the national team and I have to improve. I have to do more to make the team competitive again. We haven’t been competitive for a long time. I want to do more to make the national team the most competitive in the world.

“It is obvious that it is time for experimenting. We are testing new players. We always hope to play well, but it is incompatible to try new things and have the team ready.

“We all believe that the team is on the right track. We continue with great confidence on this path and will put ourselves to the test against Singapore. Right now, we must evaluate what we are doing well and what we need to improve. Some aspects against Japan showed that we need to evolve more in defence than in attack. But we are on the right track to have a very strong national team in the future.”

Endrick to start for Brazil against Singapore

Barcelona forward Raphinha was also dismissed against Japan, forcing Ancelotti to make at least one change in attack for the Singapore clash. And he confirmed it would mean a chance for Real Madrid’s Endrick.

He said: ”We are going to make some changes to the starting line-up, but in attack I will start with Willian Estevão, Endrick and Vinícius.”

articles.title: Not everyone can be like Messi and Ronaldo, says Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr, after admitting he partied too hard over the summer
articles.summary: Vinicius Jr has vowed to knuckle down at Real Madrid after admitting his pre-season was not perfect
articles.content:
Not everyone can be like Messi and Ronaldo, says Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr, after admitting he partied too hard over the summer

Vinicius Jr has vowed to knuckle down at Real Madrid after admitting his pre-season was not perfect

Last Update:

Vinicius Junior has attributed his slow start to the season to a lack of hard work over the summer but has vowed to get his Real Madrid career back on track.

The Brazil forward has endured a stop-start couple of months, scoring just once and adding three assists in 12 appearances in all competitions, as well as serving a four-game suspension following a red card against Villarreal.

Having been a mainstay of the Madrid side for many years, the left winger is now being challenged for his place by recent arrival Yan Diomande. The pair have played together but have yet to gel.

Vinicius signed a new, six-year contract in August after a summer that saw him suffer an earlier-than-expected exit from the World Cup with Brazil beaten by Norway in the round of 16.

And the 26-year-old, who was pictured partying with ex-girlfriend Virginia Fonseca, as well as having chin reconstruction, admits he did not knuckle down in the weeks leading up to the new La Liga campaign.

Speaking ahead of Brazil’s friendly with Singapore on Tuesday, he said: “I didn’t prepare well after the World Cup because the impact of this tournament is very significant for all Brazilians. Losing so soon was something we didn’t expect. So I took advantage of the holidays to enjoy life, rest, relax and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in recent years.

“This may have affected my start to the season. In addition, regarding the renewal of my contract, with so many clubs interested last summer, I felt really overwhelmed, as did the situation at Real Madrid. But the season is very long.”

I will be ready when it matters for Real Madrid, insist Vinicius

Vinicius was also slow out of the blocks last season but came good, and he is confident it will be the same in 2026/27.

“Last season, by December, I had only scored five goals,” he added. “But I ended up with more than 20, as in all the other seasons. I think I’m preparing, evolving, because, at the most decisive moment of the season, I’m always there.”

Vinicius joined Madrid from Flamengo in 2018 and has not endured too many slumps. And he says there are only two men that have managed to perform at the highest level over longer periods.

He said: ”Maintaining such a high level for so long is always very difficult. I think only Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi have achieved it for so many years, reaching the same figures. I’m human, I make mistakes often, but I always try to improve. I try to understand soccer better, day to day, but I’m 26 years old and I also have to enjoy life a little.”

Former Real Madrid boss Ancelotti under pressure with Brazil

Brazil were beaten by Japan at the weekend, despite Vinicius’ brace, increasing the pressure on boss Carlo Ancelotti.

“Criticism at this time is normal,” said Vinicius. “Brazil has not won a World Cup for a long time, we were eliminated very early, and it is normal for everyone to talk and give their opinion, for the players who used to play to say what they think.

“But when I look at Ronaldinho, Ronaldo… they always speak well of us. We have to listen to those who are looking out for us. We are saddened by not having achieved the results we wanted, but we are in a process of experimentation with many young players.

“The fans ask for new players, the coach brings them in, and then they complain. It’s their right. Until we find our style of play, we will suffer with this. Until the Copa America, we have to find ourselves in the best possible way. Time flies, and the Copa America will be just around the corner.”

articles.title: Thomas Tuchel hails England’s ‘best performance’ under him after stunning Spain win
articles.summary: Thomas Tuchel has called England's win over Spain his best performance as manager.
articles.content:
Thomas Tuchel hails England’s ‘best performance’ under him after stunning Spain win

Thomas Tuchel has called England's win over Spain his best performance as manager.

Last Update:

Thomas Tuchel has described England’s win over Spain as the best performance of his reign, praising his players for producing a “fantastic performance from start to finish” despite being reduced to 10 men.

The Three Lions secured a crucial Nations League win against Spain, with Tuchel insisting his side were deserved winners after dominating the opening hour.

However, the England boss questioned the decision to award Spain a penalty and show a red card in the same incident, admitting he was confused by the double punishment.

Speaking to ITV Sport after the match, Tuchel was full of praise for his players and the quality they showed against one of Europe’s strongest international sides.

“Brilliant performance. Well deserved win. Overall we were the better team. Fantastic performance from start to finish,” he said.

“A red card and penalty always a big decision. I need to understand why it was a double punishment.

“From then it was a long 30 minutes but I don’t want to focus on that. There were so many positive things in the first 60 minutes.”

Despite having to defend with 10 men for the closing stages, Tuchel believed England had already demonstrated their superiority before the dismissal.

“Complete performance. We brought everything to the table. We were brave. Spirit wise, energy wise and also football quality was highest level.

“We deserved it. We focused on our performance and attitude. I can’t praise the team high enough for what they put out there.

“Half an hour feels like two hours against a team like this [with 10 men]. That’s the way it is. Without the red card we were clear winners.”

England boss sets sights on Nations League quarter-finals

Tuchel believes England’s performance demonstrated the progress his squad have made following their World Cup campaign.

Asked what the result showed about his players, the England manager highlighted their determination to keep improving.

“What we are made of and what we can do. We are always ready to push our limits,” he said.

“We had our best result in 60 years [at the World Cup] and we weren’t happy with it. It’s impressive what we did in the last two camps.”

When asked whether the display was England’s best under his management, Tuchel seemed to think so.

“Under the circumstances against who and where we played, yeah.”

articles.title: Nations League round-up: Belgium thrash Italy as France beat Turkey
articles.summary: Catch up on Sunday's UEFA Nations League action, including Belgium's impressive win over Italy, France's meeting with Turkey and England's trip to Spain.
articles.content:
Nations League round-up: Belgium thrash Italy as France beat Turkey

Catch up on Sunday's UEFA Nations League action, including Belgium's impressive win over Italy, France's meeting with Turkey and England's trip to Spain.

Last Update:

Belgium came from behind to thrash Italy 4-1 in Brussels on Sunday evening, with Jeremy Doku among the goalscorers as the hosts finished their Nations League group campaign in style.

France also beat Turkey 2-1, while England picked up an impressive 3-2 win away to Spain in another eventful night of international football.

Belgium 4-1 Italy

Belgium scored three times in 11 first-half minutes to come from behind and beat Italy 4-1 in Brussels.

Francesco Pio Esposito gave the visitors an 11th-minute lead, turning home Luca Koleosho’s cross, but Maxim De Cuyper equalised four minutes later following a clever pass from Kevin De Bruyne.

Nathan Ngoy put Belgium ahead in the 22nd minute, reacting quickest after Gianluigi Donnarumma saved Doku’s initial effort, before the Manchester City winger produced a fine individual finish to make it 3-1.

Diego Moreira added a fourth in the 80th minute, converting from a De Bruyne assist to complete a miserable evening for the Italians.

France 2-1 Turkey

France rounded off their Nations League group campaign with a 2-1 win over Turkey in Bordeaux.

The hosts broke the deadlock four minutes after half-time when Emirhan Topcu turned the ball into his own net.

Eli Junior Kroupi doubled France’s advantage in the 80th minute, giving Didier Deschamps’ side a two-goal cushion heading into the closing stages.

Abdulkerim Bardakci pulled one back for Turkey in the 90th minute, but France held on to take all three points.

articles.title: Erling Haaland breaks silence on Man City punishment fears and insists ‘I’m incredibly happy there’
articles.summary: Erling Haaland insists he is "incredibly happy" at Manchester City despite the threat of major Premier League sanctions.
articles.content:
Erling Haaland breaks silence on Man City punishment fears and insists ‘I’m incredibly happy there’

Erling Haaland insists he is "incredibly happy" at Manchester City despite the threat of major Premier League sanctions.

Last Update:

Erling Haaland has insisted he remains “incredibly happy” at Manchester City despite the club facing potentially severe sanctions for breaching Premier League financial regulations.

City are appealing after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches, with possible punishments including a substantial points deduction or even demotion if the verdict is upheld.

However, Haaland has dismissed suggestions that the uncertainty could affect his future, pointing to the long-term contract he signed in 2024 as evidence of his commitment.

Speaking to Norwegian broadcaster TV2 after scoring in Norway’s 3-1 Nations League win over Wales, Haaland admitted he was uncomfortable discussing the ongoing legal proceedings.

“This is a question I struggle to answer, because it’s a legal battle between the Premier League and Manchester City,” he said.

“Am I supposed to answer that? I don’t really know. It’s a difficult question to answer when I don’t know that much about it.

“To be completely honest, I’m focused on trying to perform for Manchester City. A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022, and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024.

“I think that says everything about the matter. I’m a City player and I’m incredibly happy there.”

Asked directly whether the potential sanctions could influence his future, the striker made it clear he had no intention of fuelling speculation.

“I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said I signed a long-term contract in 2024,” Haaland continued.

“I’d say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that.

“I won’t say it myself, but look at the trophies I’ve won and how I’ve developed on and off the pitch.”

Man City striker focused on reversing Premier League struggles

Haaland’s comments come after an independent commission found City guilty in September, including breaches relating to the concealment of more than £830million in funding between 2009 and 2018.

City maintain they possess a “comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence” supporting their case.

Haaland stressed that the period under investigation predates his arrival at the Etihad Stadium and admitted he has not followed the proceedings closely.

“The investigation covered 2009-2018. I assume the answers will come,” he said.

“I don’t know when. I haven’t read much about it.

“I’m standing here after winning an international 3-1. Things aren’t going so well in the Premier League, but we’ll try to turn that around against Fulham [on Saturday].”

articles.title: Brazil boss Ancelotti tells Real Madrid and Barcelona to relax and insists he won’t take risks with star men
articles.summary: Barcelona and Real Madrid have expressed concern at their star players travelling to Asia during an important stage of the season but Brazil boss Carlo Ancelotti says there is no need to worry
articles.content:
Brazil boss Ancelotti tells Real Madrid and Barcelona to relax and insists he won’t take risks with star men

Barcelona and Real Madrid have expressed concern at their star players travelling to Asia during an important stage of the season but Brazil boss Carlo Ancelotti says there is no need to worry

Last Update:

Brazil boss Carlo Ancelotli has moved to allay fears from Barcelona and Real Madrid that their star players will be overworked during this international break.

Barca’s Raphinha was called up despite another injury-disrupted season while Madrid are also believed to be concerned that Vinicius Junior has had to travel to Asia for matches with Japan and Singapore.

But Ancelotti, who understands the demands on players at La Liga’s top clubs better than most after two spells in charge of Madrid, is adamant he won’t take any risks.

He said: “The priority is always the player’s health. If you’re at 100%, you train. If you’re at 100%, you play. And in this aspect, we control the minutes they play. The clubs can be calm with the national team. The priority for everyone is the health of the athlete. We always want the athlete to return prepared to play and without injuries.”

Brazil period of experimentation is coming to an end – Ancelotti

Ancelotti has named experimental squads since Brazil’s World Cup elimination against Norway in the round of 16. But he says this period of trying new players will come to an end after these two games.

“It’s a trial period that will end with this international break,” he said. “Next time, we will define the squad. It was a period that provided us with a lot of information about young players. We know now that we have very talented and committed young players, and that gives us confidence for the future. We have very high-level players. We have coverage in some positions, a little less in others, but we have time.”

While Ancelotti knows the Brazilian public have been patient over the past few months, he accepts results will be key as they start qualifying for the 2028 Copa America and the 2030 World Cup that follows.

The Italian said: ”We are dedicating all our efforts to make this period a success. It is a transitional stage for the national team, a time for new players to emerge, and that is the work we have to do. Fans must remain calm, because we are going to form a very strong group of players for the future.”

Raphinha defends Brazil commitment after criticism

Brazil take on Japan on Saturday before meeting Singapore on Tuesday.

Raphinha and Vinicius are both expected to start against the Blue Samurai with the Barcelona man having to defend himself against accusations of a lack of commitment to his country after suggesting his minutes would need to be managed.

Speaking to the media in Singapore on Friday, a visibly emotional Raphinha paused before saying: “At that moment, when they asked me the question and I answered, I thought I was being clear in what I wanted to say; at least in my head it seemed to me that I was. Taking into account everything I have been through in the last three international call-ups, with three injuries practically in the same area of the leg, what I meant was, simply, that I had to take care of myself. Obviously, I don’t want to get injured again. I want to be available not only for the national team, but also for Barcelona.”

The former Leeds man added: “From the first time I put on the national team shirt I have always made my willingness to be here very clear. I never resigned from the Brazilian national team and I always did my best to be present. Sometimes, I haven’t been able to come, but I’ve always done everything in my power to be here and wear the Seleçao shirt. For me, it has always been an honour and a privilege, and always will be. That’s not going to change, regardless of how long I’m here.”

articles.title: Pochettino breaks down in tears at emotional press conference ahead of Manchester United move
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino will start his new role at Manchester United after leading the USA in a two-legged clash with Haiti
articles.content:
Pochettino breaks down in tears at emotional press conference ahead of Manchester United move

Mauricio Pochettino will start his new role at Manchester United after leading the USA in a two-legged clash with Haiti

Last Update:

Mauricio Pochettino broke down in tears and admitted opting to leave the United States for Manchester United was “the most difficult decision in my career”.

The Argentine has accepted the role at Old Trafford and will replace Michael Carrick, who was sacked on Thursday with United in the Premier League relegation zone having won one of their first 10 games.

But he conceded he was leaving the US Soccer Federation with a heavy heart after two years in charge of the national team.

“The staff and the players, I want to say thank you so much for the last two years,” he said. “You made me feel really happy sharing an amazing project. It’s difficult now for me to finish.

“We were very excited to share a project which we really believe in and are evolving together, it makes the decision harder. It’s a sad decision but we are professionals, and we need to try to find the next step to make your dreams come true.

“I didn’t prepare a speech; I am talking from the heart. We recovered our motivation and the capacity to dig deep.

“I want to recognise the value from us and me. Big thank you. You respect your work. You never lie to us. This is a difficult decision but we need to move forward.”

Normally you cry because you are sacked, says incoming United boss Pochettino

Pochettino gathered himself and joked: “It’s not an easy decision. Normally it’s the opposite. Normally, you cry because you want to stay but it’s the opposite. We are excited for the step forward but it’s a moment for commitment because we care and we always will.

“We need to focus on the next two games because they’re important. The players are amazing. The situation is not ideal. But in life, football moves quickly. We need to move forward to keep that relationship and the memories we shared.

“It’s difficult to talk now. I’m a very emotional guy. It’s a very sad decision. It’s the most difficult decision of my career.

“But we are professionals and we are trying to make our dreams come true.”

The 54-year-old’s final two games in charge will be the two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final tie against Haiti. The first game is in Miami on Friday night and the second in Cincinnati on Tuesday.

“We have time this week to talk about the job in Manchester but I think it’s much better to talk about us, about US Soccer. We have two games ahead and now it’s focus on this,” he said, before explaining what he said to the squad.

“When things start to become big and big, players are very sensitive,” he added. “We were talking with the federation and yesterday, when the agreement was reached, we had a meeting and I communicated with the players. They were very supportive. US Soccer and Manchester United agreed we would continue [for this international break], and that will not change our commitment.”

Pochettino signed a new, four-year deal with US Soccer in August but admitted the chance to manage United was too big to turn down.

“I never said I wanted to go back [to England] but they know there aren’t too many opportunities that happen in your career like Manchester United,” he said. “When it arrives, it’s difficult to turn down.

“When we decided together to extend our commitment, it was a commitment for the federation, just in case. We were very committed. It was to help the federation, just in case that didn’t work for four years.”

Pochettino will have little time to prepare for United’s clash with Liverpool

Pochettino will fly to England next Wednesday and will have little time with his new squad prior to his first game in charge, at Liverpool a week on Sunday.

Asked why he didn’t move to United straight away, he said: “Before being professionals we are people. The emotional link between us that we built in these two years is to show the commitment and respect and the care and the love even if we took a decision that, for one party, is maybe not the best.

“We were open, you know, because I think we have the respect of the players and the staff, and they understand the situation.

“If Manchester United and the federation agreed on different terms, I would need to respect the agreement, but this has happened and of course all the games are important.”

United have agreed to pay Pochettino’s release clause of £7.4million to make him the successor to Carrick at Old Trafford.

A club statement on Friday morning read: “Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the Manchester United men’s head coach from 18 November.

“The club has reached an agreement with the US Soccer Federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the US Men’s National Team.”

United hope Pochettino will inspire improvement

Pochettino will be tasked with improving a United side that has made the club’s worst start to a top-flight season since 1986.

The United statement added: “The Argentinian is renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players.

“Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues. He began his coaching career with Espanyol in 2009 before joining Southampton and achieving a club-record Premier League points tally in 2014.

“During five full seasons at Tottenham Hotspur, Pochettino established the club as regular Champions League contenders, securing qualification in four consecutive seasons and leading the club to its first final in the competition in 2019.

“In 2021, he joined Paris Saint-Germain, where he won the Ligue 1 title, the Coupe de France and the Trophée des Champions before joining Chelsea in 2023.

“Most recently he led the US Men’s National Team to the Round of 16 at the FIFA World Cup.”

US Soccer chief hails departing Pochettino

Pochettino leaves the US with a ringing endorsement from CEO and Secretary General JT Batson after a two-year spell in which he won 21 and drew two of his 35 games in charge.

Batson told ussoccer.com: “Mauricio has left a lasting mark on US Soccer through his leadership, professionalism and commitment to our players and culture

“What we are most proud of goes beyond the wins. He and his staff raised standards, strengthened our culture and created clearer connections from the youth national teams to the senior team. Those changes are now embedded in how we operate, and we will keep building on them as we pursue sustained success on the world stage.”

United will also hope Pochettino can follow in the club’s traditions of bringing through young players, as he has with the US with the likes of 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan and 17-year-old Mathis Albert getting their first goals in impressive recent wins over Chile and Mexico.

Pochettino will be followed to United by his long-time assistant Jesus Perez and the rest of his staff.

What now for the US?

Steve Cherundolo will lead the scheduled camp in December while the process to find a new head coach gets underway, led by the soccer leadership team at US Soccer that includes Emma Hayes and former USMNT defender Oguchi Onyewu.

Batson added: “With the great combination of veterans, fantastic young talent and a world-class facility, we are confident in the future of this program

“We are looking for a leader with the talent, experience and belief to match our ambition, build on the culture and pathway now in place and help the USMNT take the next step.”

articles.title: Tottenham boss De Zerbi wins manager of the month award with Jackson and Gomez also recognised
articles.summary: Roberto De Zerbi has been rewarded for guiding Tottenham off the foot of the Premier League table with the manager of the month award
articles.content:
Tottenham boss De Zerbi wins manager of the month award with Jackson and Gomez also recognised

Roberto De Zerbi has been rewarded for guiding Tottenham off the foot of the Premier League table with the manager of the month award

Last Update:

Roberto De Zerbi has been named Premier League Manager of the Month for masterminding Tottenham’s move off the foot of the table.

Spurs went into October rock bottom and without a win but now sit 11th after a draw at Manchester United was followed by victories over Coventry, Chelsea and Crystal Palace.

They lost their last outing at Leeds on November 7 but can finally look forward after a dismal couple of seasons.

De Zerbi is the first Tottenham boss to win the award since Ange Postecoglou, who claimed it in August, September and October 2023.

The Italian said: “I feel good. I’m happy. I want to say thanks to my players, for my club because it’s not my credit. But, when you are a coach, you work with many, many people and it’s right to say thanks to everybody.”

Villa goal machine Jackson named best player for October

Aston Villa striker Nicolas Jackson won the player of the month award after scoring four times.

The Senegal international netted the equaliser in a 2-2 draw with Brentford, got both goals in a famous 2-1 victory over Manchester City and also scored in the 1-1 draw with Fulham.

Best goal was awarded to Diego Gomez for his 51.3 metre effort for Brighton in the 5-0 hammering of Crystal Palace.

Gomez netted the Seagulls’ second on a memorable afternoon as they put their M23 rivals to the sword at the Amex.

It was the longest distance a Premier League goal had been scored from since Wayne Rooney’s 57.7m effort for Eveton against West Ham United in 2017.

articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino will succeed Michael Carrick at Manchester United
articles.content:
Manchester United confirm Pochettino as new boss

Mauricio Pochettino will succeed Michael Carrick at Manchester United

Last Update:

Manchester United have confirmed the appointment of Mauricio Pochettino as the club’s new head coach.

The Argentine will leave his role in charge of the United States men’s team to move to Old Trafford at the conclusion of this international window. Pochettino will, therefore, be in charge for the States’ two-legged tie with Haiti before leaving for England.

The second leg takes place in Cincinnati on Tuesday, November 17, leaving Pochettino with little time to get to know the United squad before they return to Premier League action with a trip to arch-rivals Liverpool on Sunday, November 22.

United have agreed to pay Pochettino’s release clause of £7.4million to make him the successor to Michael Carrick, who was sacked on Thursday.

A club statement read: “Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the Manchester United men’s head coach from 18 November.

“The club has reached an agreement with the US Soccer Federation for Mauricio and his staff to be released after the conclusion of their responsibilities with the US Men’s National Team.”

United hope Pochettino will inspire improvement

Pochettino will be tasked with improving a United side that has won just one of their opening 10 Premier League games and currently sits inside the relegation zone having made their worst start to a top-flight season since 1986.

The United statement added: “The Argentinian is renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players.

“Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues. He began his coaching career with Espanyol in 2009 before joining Southampton and achieving a club-record Premier League points tally in 2014.

“During five full seasons at Tottenham Hotspur, Pochettino established the club as regular Champions League contenders, securing qualification in four consecutive seasons and leading the club to its first final in the competition in 2019.

“In 2021, he joined Paris Saint-Germain, where he won the Ligue 1 title, the Coupe de France and the Trophée des Champions before joining Chelsea in 2023.

“Most recently he led the US Men’s National Team to the Round of 16 at the FIFA World Cup.”

US Soccer chief hails departing Pochettino

Pochettino leaves the US with a ringing endorsement from CEO and Secretary General JT Batson after a two-year spell in which he won 21 and drew two of his 35 games in charge.

Batson told ussoccer.com: “Mauricio has left a lasting mark on US Soccer through his leadership, professionalism and commitment to our players and culture

“What we are most proud of goes beyond the wins. He and his staff raised standards, strengthened our culture and created clearer connections from the youth national teams to the senior team. Those changes are now embedded in how we operate, and we will keep building on them as we pursue sustained success on the world stage.”

Carrick sacked by United after dismal start

Carrick took over on an interim basis in January, succeeding Ruben Amorim, and inspired a dramatic uptick in performances that resulted in a third-placed finish and qualification for the Champions League.

He was rewarded with a two-year deal but this season has not gone to plan. That is in part due to an underwhelming summer of recruitment by director of football Jason Wilcox in which United bolstered the midfield with the likes of Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos but left the squad short in other areas, most notably left back and attack.

They are now Pochettino’s problems to solve, along with a dressing room that has appeared to put individual interests ahead of the greater good at times this season with two senior players making unwanted public statements. The first saw Argentina defend Lisandro Martinez criticise the club hierarchy following the defeat at Atletico Madrid while captain Bruno Fernandes questioned Carrick’s tactics after the 4-1 thrashing in Como.

United will also hope Pochettino can follow in the club’s traditions of bringing through young players, as he has with the US with the likes of 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan and 17-year-old Mathis Albert getting their first goals in impressive wins over Chile and Mexico.

Pochettino will be followed to United by his long-time assistant Jesus Perez and the rest of his staff.

The 54-year-old said: “The opportunity to represent the USA crest was one of the greatest honours of my career. We are so grateful to the players for their commitment, to the fans for their belief, and to the Federation for always supporting our staff and creating the opportunities to impact the culture of soccer in this great country.

“There is tremendous talent in the US player pool from the youth teams through to the senior team, and it’s one of the reasons we have so much belief for the future of US Soccer. You will always have a special place in our hearts, and we will be supporting the teams whenever they step on the field.”

What now for the US?

Steve Cherundolo will lead the scheduled camp in December while the process to find a new head coach gets underway, led by the soccer leadership team at US Soccer that includes Emma Hayes and former USMNT defender Oguchi Onyewu.

Batson added: “With the great combination of veterans, fantastic young talent and a world-class facility, we are confident in the future of this program

“We are looking for a leader with the talent, experience and belief to match our ambition, build on the culture and pathway now in place and help the USMNT take the next step.”

articles.title: Michael Carrick breaks his silence and pens emotional message to Manchester United supporters
articles.summary: Michael Carrick has left an emotional message for Manchester United fans after being sacked on Thursday
articles.content:
Michael Carrick breaks his silence and pens emotional message to Manchester United supporters

Michael Carrick has left an emotional message for Manchester United fans after being sacked on Thursday

Last Update:

Michael Carrick has thanked the Manchester United players and supporters in an emotional message following his sacking on Thursday.

Carrick was dismissed with United in the Premier League relegation zone having won one of their opening 10 games – the club’s worst start to a season since 1986. It was confirmed this morning that Mauricio Pochettino will replace him at Old Trafford.

Despite the club’s struggles on the field, the supporters continued to back Carrick, who won five Premier League crowns with United as a player under Sir Alex Ferguson, and the 45-year-old admitted he had been touched by their relentless backing.

A post shared by Michael Carrick (@carras16)

In a message on Instagram, he wrote: “I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love. There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful.

“With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. It’s different to anywhere else.

“Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time.

“It’s a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored. This is what inspired me every single day.

“I want to say a big thank you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed. We’ve had some great times this year and moments we’ll all remember. The best thing about being in my position was seeing many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time.

“I just wanted to give you something back. That love never dies.

“I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way. That means more than a win or two. That’s what makes you who you are. That’s why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.”

Carrick thanks United staff and players

Carrick thanked his staff, who also left the club on Thursday, as well as the squad.

He added: “A special thank you to my coaching staff. You gave me everything you had, every single day, and I couldn’t have asked for any more. I’m incredibly grateful for your loyalty, hard work and support throughout.

“To all the staff behind the scenes, thank you for everything you do for this football club. So much of your work goes unseen, but it never goes unappreciated.

“And to the players, thank you for your efforts and the moments we’ve shared. I wish you all the very best for what’s ahead.

“I want nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change. I’ll always be proud to have played my part and I’ll always want the very best for it.

“I’ll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on.”

articles.title: Former team-mate says Cristiano Ronaldo is “misunderstood” as striker prepares to watch Portugal from afar after international retirement
articles.summary: Portugal will play their first game following the international retirement of Cristiano Ronaldo on Saturday when they face Denmark
articles.content:
Former team-mate says Cristiano Ronaldo is “misunderstood” as striker prepares to watch Portugal from afar after international retirement

Portugal will play their first game following the international retirement of Cristiano Ronaldo on Saturday when they face Denmark

Last Update:

A former team-mate of Cristiano Ronaldo says the Al-Nassr striker is “misunderstood” and won’t be replaced overnight in the Portugal squad.

Ronaldo will not be present when Portugal resume their Nations League campaign on Saturday with a game against Denmark having retired from international football after clashing with coach Jorge Jesus.

And Adrien Silva, who played alongside Ronaldo for the national team, believes it is a huge blow.

Silva told Kooora: “You can’t replace a player like Ronaldo quickly. You cannot replace overnight a figure with the historical impact of the magnitude of Cristiano.”

Ronaldo was not arrogant, he had enormous self-confidence – Silva

Ronaldo’s decision to quit the international game was prompted by a row that escalated when he was left on the bench by Jesus for the game with Norway. The 41-year-old left the squad and flew home on his private jet.

His actions sparked accusations of arrogance but Silva, who played for Sporting CP and Leicester among others and was part of the Portugal squad that won Euro 2016, says they are misplaced.

“Sometimes, his enormous self-confidence is misunderstood. Anyone who competes at the highest level needs to believe in themselves unconditionally,” he said. “What some described as arrogance was just real ambition and the natural frustration of someone who hates losing.

“Cristiano Ronaldo earned his status on the field, through his performance, his titles and his commitment to his country. He was always the first to lead by example through his hard work, his punctuality and his dedication.

“When your leader is the person who works with the maximum effort, that naturally wins the admiration of the whole group.”

Ronaldo’s absence from the last three games has not hindered Portugal and they top Nations League group A4 having won all four fixtures.

And Silva believes the future is still bright.

He said: “Portugal currently has an exceptional generation of talent, developed through the excellent work of the clubs and the federation.

“There is enough quality and maturity to build a strong and united team, capable of continuing to compete for the greatest titles on the world scene.”

Portugal will still challenge, even without Ronaldo

Real Madrid midfielder Bernardo Silva will wear the captain’s armband against Denmark and Silva believes there are enough experienced players in the squad to compensate for the leadership lost following Ronaldo’s departure.

“Portugal are still in a very strong position,” he said. “Players like Rúben Dias, Bruno Fernandes and Bernardo Silva have demonstrated leadership, personality and tactical intelligence on the biggest stages of world football for several years. Without a doubt, there will be no problem.”

Ronaldo will spend the international break working on other ventures, including starring in a new drama that explores the world of transfers.

Ronaldo will appear as himself in the series, which is being produced through UR Marv Studios, the production company he co-founded with British filmmaker Matthew Vaughn.

The former Manchester United and Real Madrid forward will also serve as an executive producer.

articles.title: Barcelona star Raphinha holds back tears as he defends his commitment to Brazil
articles.summary: Raphinha admitted to have been affected by the backlash to his words in Brazil
articles.content:
Barcelona star Raphinha holds back tears as he defends his commitment to Brazil

Raphinha admitted to have been affected by the backlash to his words in Brazil

Last Update:

Raphinha has outlined his commitment to Brazil but stressed he wants to play injury-free for the national team and Barcelona.

The 29-year-old received criticism in his homeland when he suggested he had spoken to Brazil boss Carlo Ancelotti and they had agreed to manage his minutes during the upcoming international friendlies with Japan and Singapore.

But the Barca forward insisted he was not prioritising club over country and was simply explaining he has to look after his body.

Speaking to the media in Singapore, a visibly emotional Raphinha paused before saying: “At that moment, when they asked me the question and I answered, I thought I was being clear in what I wanted to say; at least in my head it seemed to me that I was. Taking into account everything I have been through in the last three international call-ups, with three injuries practically in the same area of the leg, what I meant was, simply, that I had to take care of myself. Obviously, I don’t want to get injured again. I want to be available not only for the national team, but also for Barcelona.”

The former Leeds man added: “From the first time I put on the national team shirt I have always made my willingness to be here very clear. I never resigned from the Brazilian national team and I always did my best to be present. Sometimes, I haven’t been able to come, but I’ve always done everything in my power to be here and wear the Seleçao shirt. For me, it has always been an honour and a privilege, and always will be. That’s not going to change, regardless of how long I’m here.”

Brazil barbs stung, admits Raphinha

Raphinha admitted he had been stung by the criticism back home.

“We are human beings and, no matter how hard we try, some things affect us,” he said. “It’s natural. Anyone in my place, receiving criticism knowing that they are giving everything, would be affected. We have to be prepared for criticism, defending Brazil is something very big.”

Raphinha will win his 43rd cap for Brazil tomorrow and wear the captain’s armband but warned he would step away from the national team if he felt he could no longer perform to his best level.

He said: ”Unfortunately, when we are not physically well we cannot play either here or at the club. I also said that, if my body allows me, I will always give my best. When I see that I can’t physically perform, I’ll be the first to retire, because I’m very critical of myself.

“Yes, what I said had a bad impact, although at the time I thought I had explained it well. But it’s part of the game unfortunately.”

Brazil boss Ancelotti sticks up for captain Raphinha

Ancelotti has no doubts over Raphinha’s commitment and gave a glowing assessment of his captain ahead of the game with Japan.

He said: “I know the players want to play for the national team and I don’t need to say anything to them to get them out there competing.

“Brazil is the greatest national team in the world and the fans will be right behind us in every match and will support us. It’s different in other countries.”

Raphinha has been in blistering form for the Blaugrana this season with 15 goals in 11 La Liga games having been moved into a number nine position by Hansi Flick. He helped his side establish a three-point lead over Real Madrid heading into the international break. They return to Liga action a week on Sunday with a home game against Villarreal.

articles.title: Harry Kane sends Spain warning as England captain vows to ‘prove ourselves’ in Nations League showdown
articles.summary: Harry Kane insists England have the 'perfect opportunity' to prove themselves against Spain on Sunday after scoring from the penalty spot in their latest win.
articles.content:
Harry Kane sends Spain warning as England captain vows to ‘prove ourselves’ in Nations League showdown

Harry Kane insists England have the 'perfect opportunity' to prove themselves against Spain on Sunday after scoring from the penalty spot in their latest win.

Last Update:

Harry Kane has set his sights on beating Spain and finishing top of England’s Nations League group after helping the Three Lions secure another important win on Thursday night.

The England captain converted from the penalty spot on a night he became England’s most-capped player in a 2-1 win over Croatia to book their place in the quarter-finals.

Speaking to ITV after the match, Kane made it clear that beating Spain and topping the group is a major target for England.

“100%. After the first game when we lost here against them, we knew we left a bit out there,” he said.

“We knew we could’ve done a bit better. We said to ourselves let’s win every game until the next one and see what happens.

“It’s the perfect opportunity now on Sunday to try and prove ourselves.”

The Bayern Munich striker was pleased with England’s performance on Thursday, although he admitted there were areas that needed improving ahead of the showdown.

“An incredible gesture, reception at the start of the game,” Kane said.

“Once the game starts, it’s about getting the win, getting the three points. We’re playing against a tough team, a team that wanted to prove something tonight.

“I think for large spells of the game we done well. Got a little bit tired towards the end but overall a really great win and sets up a great game on Sunday now.”

England captain explains penalty mindset after Bayern miss

Kane also discussed his successful penalty, revealing he was particularly determined to score after missing his previous spot-kick for Bayern Munich.

“Same as ever. I missed my last one for Bayern, so I think it’s always important to try and bounce back with the next one,” he explained.

“Try to not miss two in a row but executing. I practiced yesterday like I always do and it’s just about going out there and doing it out on the pitch.”

articles.title: Nations League round-up: Spain beat Czech Republic as Belgium edge Turkey and Albania see off Finland
articles.summary: Catch up on Thursday night's UEFA Nations League action, including Spain's trip to Czech Republic, Turkey against Belgium and Albania's meeting with Finland.
articles.content:
Nations League round-up: Spain beat Czech Republic as Belgium edge Turkey and Albania see off Finland

Catch up on Thursday night's UEFA Nations League action, including Spain's trip to Czech Republic, Turkey against Belgium and Albania's meeting with Finland.

Last Update:

The UEFA Nations League continued on Thursday evening with eight matches taking place across Europe as teams entered the final stages of the league phase.

Spain travelled to Czech Republic looking to maintain their impressive form, while Belgium faced Turkey and Finland took on Albania.

England were also in action against Croatia, with Italy hosting France in another heavyweight League A encounter.

Here is how things unfolded.

Czech Republic 0-2 Spain

Alex Baena and Marc Pubill were on target as Spain beat Czech Republic 2-0 in Prague to maintain their perfect record in the Nations League.

Baena opened the scoring from the penalty spot in the 39th minute, giving Luis de la Fuente’s side a half-time advantage.

The visitors had to wait until the sixth minute of stoppage time to double their lead, with Pubill finding the net to put the result beyond doubt.

Spain now head into Sunday’s meeting with England knowing a draw will be enough to finish top of their League A group.

Turkey 1-2 Belgium

Kevin De Bruyne and Charles De Ketelaere scored three minutes apart as Belgium came from behind to beat Turkey 2-1 in Izmir.

Real Madrid midfielder Arda Guler gave the hosts the lead in the 20th minute, but De Bruyne equalised just seven minutes later.

De Ketelaere completed the turnaround in the 30th minute, leaving Turkey trailing at half-time despite their promising start.

Belgium held on to take all three points ahead of their final group fixture against Italy on Sunday.

Albania 2-0 Finland

Ernest Muci and Olsi Manj scored either side of half-time as Albania beat Finland 2-0 in Tirana.

Muci broke the deadlock in the 35th minute to put the hosts ahead following a competitive opening half-hour.

Manj doubled Albania’s advantage five minutes after the restart, leaving Finland with a difficult task in the second half.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces ‘exciting news’ as football icon begins filming first TV series alongside Hollywood stars
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo confirms filming has begun on his first TV series, Day 1s, featuring Damian Lewis, rapper Dave and Arsenal legend Thierry Henry.
articles.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo announces ‘exciting news’ as football icon begins filming first TV series alongside Hollywood stars

Cristiano Ronaldo confirms filming has begun on his first TV series, Day 1s, featuring Damian Lewis, rapper Dave and Arsenal legend Thierry Henry.

Last Update:

Cristiano Ronaldo has confirmed that production has begun on his first television series, with the football legend set to appear alongside a star-studded cast in a new drama exploring the world of football transfers.

The 41-year-old, who recently retired from international football with Portugal, is expanding his business interests through a new project titled Day 1s.

Ronaldo will appear as himself in the series, which is being produced through UR Marv Studios, the production company he co-founded with British filmmaker Matthew Vaughn.

The former Manchester United and Real Madrid forward will also serve as an executive producer.

Ronaldo confirms filming has started on ‘Day 1s’

Ronaldo announced the news to his 681 million Instagram followers, sharing several behind-the-scenes photographs from the production.

“Exciting news! Production of my first TV show, Day 1s, has just started. More to come!” he wrote.

Among the photographs shared by Ronaldo was an image featuring British actor Damian Lewis alongside rapper Dave, both of whom are involved in the project.

Another picture showed the dressing room at Brentford, suggesting the Premier League club’s facilities will feature in the production.

The series follows the fictional story of Stanley Dalton, a British football agent played by Lewis, as he navigates the high-pressure world of player transfers and football business.

Thierry Henry joins Ronaldo in football drama

Ronaldo will not be the only legendary footballer appearing in Day 1s, with former Arsenal and France striker Thierry Henry also confirmed to feature as himself.

The involvement of two of football’s most recognisable names adds another dimension to a series centred on the business of the sport.

Vaughn, who is known for directing films including Kingsman: The Secret Service and Kick-Ass, is working with Ronaldo through their joint production venture, UR Marv Studios.

articles.title: Rio Ferdinand is right, Manchester United are a laughing stock and appointing a new ringmaster won’t make it less of a circus
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino is set to take over as Manchester United boss from the sacked Michael Carrick. But will it make any difference?
articles.content:
Rio Ferdinand is right, Manchester United are a laughing stock and appointing a new ringmaster won’t make it less of a circus

Mauricio Pochettino is set to take over as Manchester United boss from the sacked Michael Carrick. But will it make any difference?

Last Update:

Rio Ferdinand is rarely the sensible voice in the room but his description of Manchester United as a “laughing stock” is spot on as the once-great Old Trafford club lurch from one crisis to the next.

If you needed any convincing that co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, CEO Omar Berrada and sporting director Jason Wilcox were not suitable to run an historic sporting institution then the events of the past fortnight provide ample evidence.

The fall guy is Michael Carrick, this morning sacked from his role as United head coach. Did Carrick deserve to stay on with the club in the Premier League relegation zone having won one of their opening 10 games – their worst start since 1986? No, probably not.

But what he definitely did not deserve was a shambolic departure that saw The Three Stooges (AKA Ratcliffe, Berrada and Wilcox) convene in Monaco to apparently discuss the way forward while the whole world knew what was coming next via leaks and media briefings.

It all meant this morning’s announcement was inevitable and came not long after Carrick was seen leaving the Carrington training ground after reporting for duty for the third morning on the trot while his future was being debated elsewhere.

The speed at which Mauricio Pochettino has been lined up as his successor also suggests Ratcliffe and Co had made their minds up long before they had the decency to inform the former United and England midfielder.

Speaking on YouTube, Ferdinand said: “It is tiring, imagine being a player at the club right now. There is just nothing positive to say about Manchester United.

“The spotlight is on them and they don’t want it to be. United have become a laughing stock.

“The way in which it has been done could have been better and the leaks that have been coming out are terrible and it adds to the disrespect for this situation on him [Carrick] and his family. Even his kids will be feeling this. The minimum he should be getting is respect.”

United great Schmeichel angry at Carrick treatment

Respect is a trait United used to be renown for but not any more. Not since Ratcliffe bought in alongside the Glazers, promising much and delivering mass redundancies, draconian ticket policies that have alienated long-standing supporters, and one of the worst teams in the top flight.

Another United great Peter Schmeichel was also disgusted with how the hierarchy have treated a man who won five Premier League titles and the 2008 Champions League crown under Sir Alex Ferguson.

The Dane told Sky Vegas: “Do you think these people know [Carrick’s record]? Do you think they care? These people are not Manchester United people. They don’t understand what it’s like to be one of the Manchester United people. They don’t know that.

“This is obviously part of the broader issue here, part of the reason the club is where they are now. I’m not saying I feel sorry for Michael, but I’m a little bit angry at how this great football club is treating one of its greatest players. Simple as that.”

Pochettino will be installed prior to United’s next game, away at arch-rivals Liverpool a week on Sunday, and once the paperwork has been completed to extricate him from his contract with US Soccer. A trip to Anfield is  hardly the quiet start he would have wanted as he attempts to succeed where the likes of David Moyes, Louis van Gaal, Jose Mourinho, Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim have failed.

The Argentine has spoken to United on numerous occasions previously about the role but has always been overlooked. Now 54 years of age, he seems on the way down, a bit of a journeyman, rather than the upstart who guided Tottenham to the 2019 Champions League final with a brilliant young team that played with verve and vigour.

United need an overhaul but, most of all, they need the Glazers to sell

Verve and vigour are certainly not characteristics he will find on his arrival at Carrington.

Instead, he will inherit a stodgy squad high on ponderous midfielders and low on quality defenders and strikers.

United need a huge overhaul in playing personnel. The problem is that will be overseen by Wilcox, whose previous hits include spending a combined £157million this summer on Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba. That meant the team went into the season with one specialist left-back in Luke Shaw – yes, the perennially injured Luke Shaw who has made just five appearances this season – and no back-up to striker Benjamin Sesko, whose body is also made of glass.

So, incompetent sporting director, out-of-his-depth CEO and a squad high on egos but low on ability. It’s not the most appealing of positions for Pochettino to take up, and we haven’t even addressed the biggest issue he will encounter.

The stench of the Glazer family has permeated every corner of Old Trafford since Malcolm Glazer bought his first share in 2003. Thanks to the row between John Magnier and Ferguson over the race horse Rock of Gibraltar, the door opened for Glazer to seize majority control in 2005.

Ferguson’s brilliance meant trophies kept on arriving but the nature of Glazer’s leveraged buyout meant it was inevitable that would eventually stop.

Fast forward to 2026 and there is a sense of futility to sacking Carrick and bringing in Pochettino. Like shuffling deckchairs on the Titanic.

The BBC carried out some Vox pops outside Old Trafford this morning to ask fans their feelings on Carrick’s departure.

Asked if would make any difference, one lady said: “No, not in my opinion.”

Another man added: “I don’t actually think that there is a single manager in world football that could take that football club from where they are now to a better position. Before the owners go, there’s no point in getting a new manager. You might as well just get the coach from the Under-21s and put him in the football club.”

Same circus, new ringmaster. Good luck Mauricio.

articles.title: Crystal Palace sack Sage
articles.summary: Pierre Sage has been sacked by Crystal Palace with the club bottom of the Premier League
articles.content:
Crystal Palace sack Sage

Pierre Sage has been sacked by Crystal Palace with the club bottom of the Premier League

Last Update:

Crystal Palace have confirmed the sacking of manager Pierre Sage.

The Frenchman joined the Eagles in the summer as the replacement for Oliver Glasner but has failed to make a positive impression and departs Selhurst Park with Palace bottom of the Premier League table.

Sage got the Palace job after a superb 12-month stint at Lens in which he guided the club to a second-place finish in Ligue 1 last season. They also won the Coupe de France for the first time in their history.

But it has not worked out for him in South London. Palace have taken just seven points from their first 10 Premier League games and also suffered a damaging 5-0 hammering at M23 rivals Brighton last month.

Results have also been mixed in the Europa League with one win in four outings.

Sage’s staff also leave Palace

A club statement read: “Crystal Palace Football Club can confirm that Pierre Sage has left his role as manager.

“Three members of Pierre’s coaching staff – Jamal Alioui, Damien Della Santa and Sandy Guichard – have also left the club.

“The club would like to place on record its thanks to Pierre and his staff for their efforts during their time in South London, and wish them well for the future.

“An update on the process of appointing a new manager will be provided in due course.”

Frank the favourite for Palace job

Thomas Frank is the odds-on favourite to take over. The Dane has been out of work since being sacked by Tottenham in February and is believed to be eager to succeed Sage.

Reports suggest negotiations are at an advanced stage and he could be appointed prior to Palace’s trip to Coventry a week on Saturday.

Frank flopped at Spurs but made his name during an impressive spell at Brentford, during which he helped establish the Bees as one of the most progressive clubs in the Premier League.

Sage is expected to find a new role quickly having been linked with a return to Lens following the dismissal of Yannick Cahuzac on Tuesday. Lens owner and president Joseph Oughourlian is known to have retained a close bond with Sage.

articles.title: FC Andorra give Owono time to decide if he wants to return following De Miguel death
articles.summary: Jesus Owono caused the death of Jesus de Miguel after catching the Tenerife forward in the chest in a Segunda Division game
articles.content:
FC Andorra give Owono time to decide if he wants to return following De Miguel death

Jesus Owono caused the death of Jesus de Miguel after catching the Tenerife forward in the chest in a Segunda Division game

Last Update:

FC Andorra coach Carles Manso says the club will allow goalkeeper Jesus Owono to decide if he wants to return to professional football following the death of Jesus de Miguel.

Tenerife forward De Miguel died after being caught by Owono with a reckless challenge in the Segunda Division clash between the sides on November 2.

Spanish police have opened an investigation into the death but it is thought extremely unlikely any formal charges against Owono will follow.

Andorra return to action this weekend with a game against Almeria but Owono won’t be there, having been given more time to come to terms with the situation with his family.

Manso says the Equatorial Guinea international will be welcomed back if he decides he wants to play football again.

He said: “Obviously, he is struggling with everything that has happened. It is a tragedy and in no way did he intend that to be the outcome. It is a very sensitive situation, a situation that we do not want anyone to go through.

“He, as the main one involved, has a very complicated issue to manage and we must respect his process and his privacy. Right now we know that he is with his family, his people, friends and his partner. With this, and little by little, we hope that it will help him to cope with the situation in a better way.

“It is obvious that right now he is living the worst moment of his life. All we have to do is be close to him and try to give him the maximum support possible.

“We will give him the space to feel totally free to make any decision about wanting to return, and when, or not wanting to return.”

Andorra squad have trained on a volunteer basis after incident

The incident has had a profound effect on the FC Andorra squad in general, as Manso explained.

“The truth is that it is not easy to manage the situation because no-one teaches you to experience these things,” he added. “But we are trying to approach it with common sense, try to respect the processes of each person, of each player, and make available to them psychological help or whatever they need.

“The first thing is the group, being united, because we believe that it is something that we must live together, and then that everyone has the opportunity to do it individually.”

Andorra have left it to each individual to decide if they have wanted to train over the past 10 days.

“We want everyone to have the tools to try, little by little, to return to normal,” said Manso. “In the end, the competition forces you to keep going and we have had to go back to work. But it is true that last week, above all, we tried to do volunteer training so that everyone felt free to decide. And to give the players the option to try to live these moments all together, to try to get everyone out of the house so that for those two or three hours of training they were as far away as possible from everything that had happened.”

FC Andorra boss sends message of support to De Miguel’s family

Manso was also eager to send a message of support to De Miguel’s family at this difficult time.

“I want to remember Jesús de Miguel’s family, the whole club, Tenerife and the whole island,” he said. “From here, once again and publicly, we want to send you a very strong hug and a lot of love for the situation they are also experiencing, specifically to the family, the parents, his [De Miguel’s] partner and their daughter.

“They are very hard times and from the Andorra Football Club we want to send you that hug and the maximum possible support.”
